sq.q: What is LRU approximation? Name one method used for it.
answer: LRU Approximation is a method to implement Least Recently Used behavior without full tracking of page access history (which is costly). One method is the Second-Chance (Clock) Algorithm , where each page is given a second chance before replacement based on a reference bit . Mark Allocation:

lq.q: What is thrashing in virtual memory management? Explain the causes , symptoms , effects , and methods to prevent thrashing . Support your answer with a diagram or table
answer: Thrashing is a condition in a virtual memory system where a process spends more time swapping pages in and out of memory (handling page faults ) than executing actual instructions. (20%)
Thrashing occurs when:
The degree of multiprogramming (number of processes in memory) is too high.
The degree of multiprogramming (number of processes in memory) is too high.
Each process doesn’t get enough frames to hold its working set (the pages it frequently uses).

This causes frequent page faults , leading to constant disk I/O and very poor CPU utilization .
